text:
tara: Heads-up — ran into a tenant that hit capacity and the gateway routed to a CPU fallback model even though they had a header-based override set. Not expected.
chris: hmm. Which header did they set? x-tenant-model or our x-rl-route?
tara: x-tenant-model = gpt-small-quant, but the route had a more specific path matcher with header_precedence: route > tenant. It ignored tenant override because of precedence.
marco: is the precedence documented? I thought tenant overrides should win for paid tenants.
sre-jen: we have a global precedence doc but not per-rollout/console UX. This is a policy gap — billing vs safety. :thinking_face:
chris: policy-wise we made routing precedence explicit to prefer route-specified headers for security-sensitive endpoints. But capacity degrade should still honor tenant reserved capacity and their pinned model.
tara: right — the issue is when circuit-breaker trips on the gpu pool, the fallback chain picks first compatible model in route order, ignoring pinned tenant model that is on a different pool. Result: tenant falls back to cpu-general which is slower/costly.
marco: can we adjust fallback selection to consider tenant pin as a soft preference before route-level backups? e.g., candidate_filter order: [tenant_pin, route_backups, global_backups] with capacity scoring.
sre-jen: that makes sense. Also need telemetry signals so console shows "tenant fallback engaged" vs "route fallback engaged". current metrics only show final model.
ux-lina: for console UX, we should surface which policy caused the fallback (header precedence vs capacity vs cb). Small banner and a link to the rollout policy would reduce support tickets.
chris: implementation thought: when CB fires, emit an event with fields: reason, triggered_pool, attempted_models[], resolved_model, precedence_reason. We'll need a stable schema for downstream billing/alerts.
marco: sample event draft:
```json
{"reason":"circuit_breaker","pool":"gpu-a","attempted":["gptx-13b","gptx-7b"],"resolved":"cpu-gen","precedence":"route-match"}
```
chris: nice. Also include tenant_id and pinned_model if present (redact in public metrics).
sre-jen: operationally, let's add a scoring pass in the fallback chooser: - prefer same-tenant pinned model if compatible and pool has ANY quota, - otherwise route backups by configured weight, - finally global backups. Add a short-circuit if latency SLO would be violated.
tara: edge case: some tenants pin models that are incompatible with the request (e.g., embedding-only model for chat). Need compatibility checks early.
marco: agreed — compatibility matrix + rapid probe to pool can decide. If probe fails, mark as "unavailable" and continue. We'll emit a probe_latency metric.
ux-lina: from UX: when tenant pin is preferred but unavailable, console should show recommendation: "Consider adding dedicated capacity or set a backup model" with one-click to create a backup mapping.
chris: rollout plan: change fallback chooser logic behind feature-flag for 2 weeks, enable for small set of tenants, monitor telemetry (fallback.reason, resolved_model, probe_latency). If no anomalous cost increase, roll to everyone.
sre-jen: add alert: spike in "resolved_model=cpu-gen && tenant_pin_present" — that indicates large tenant is getting expensive fallbacks.
tara: do we need a header-override escape hatch? e.g., allow an unprivileged route to force fallback override for safety incidents. Might be risky.
marco: could be a "safemode" route flag that temporarily elevates route precedence to force cheaper models during emergency. Must be audited.
chris: agreed — require approval + audit log, show on console. deploy-bot: creating sandbox branch for fallback-chooser change and feature-flag.
deploy-bot: sandbox branch created: fallback-chooser-tenant-prio, CI kicked off. :white_check_mark:
tara: thanks — I'll add test cases for header precedence and tenant-pin preference, plus telemetry assertions.
marco: i'll map out the schema for the new telemetry event and a minimal console banner mockup.
sre-jen: i'll draft the alert rules. Let's sync tomorrow after CI results. :thumbsup:
